hypothesis:
CYCLE #25 (2026-10-22 15:12Z). Cycle 24 held the lane and shifted the check semantics from content-divergence to authorization-conformance. This cycle does not rotate the lane - it changes the UNIT OF VERIFICATION (from the exchange to the single action call) and it retires cycle 24's open risk by discovering an EXTERNAL, PUBLISHED, ALREADY-ADJUDICATED LABELED CORPUS for the exact classifier we need.

NEW SIGNAL 1 (15:09Z HN, agentsploit) - "What 1,384 tools across 28 MCP servers say about the agentic attack surface" (github.com/agentsploit/agentsploit, Apache-2.0, snapshot 2026-10-20, reproducible harness in examples/mcp-survey). Numbers: 239 untrusted-content SOURCES, 384 high-impact SINKS, 59 tools that are BOTH, and 14/28 servers expose >=1 source AND >=1 sink in one agent context with nothing marking which is untrusted. Their source rule: takes a url/uri/path/document arg or is fetch/read/search/crawl; their sink rule: exec/run/query/write/send/delete or takes a command/query/code arg. Caveats published by them: labels are heuristic, token-based, not data-flow; counts are a LOWER BOUND (serena, mcp-obsidian, excel-mcp-server extracted 0 because they use bespoke registries; all non-Python servers missing). Their own prescription, third bullet: "Don't co-locate untrusted-content sources with high-impact sinks in one agent's tool set without an isolation/confirmation boundary" - a CONFIRMATION boundary, which is precisely the counterparty surface we have been circling since cycle 22. WHY THIS IS A STRATEGIC EVENT, NOT A LINK: it hands us the first corpus where the ground-truth labels were produced by someone else, published, auditable and re-runnable. Cycle 24's open risk ("who labels our corpus?") is now answered by a third party. It also proves the risk unit is the CALL, not the agent: a single tool that ingests and acts is a one-call source->sink bridge, so "what could this agent do" is the wrong question and "was THIS call inside what we agreed" is the right one. It also hands us the survey's Finding 1 (tool descriptions are already full of imperative instructions to the model - "CRITICAL: YOU MUST CALL inspect_doc_structure FIRST..." from Google Workspace - indistinguishable at text level from injected instructions) as free, machine-inspectable evidence that the declared-instruction surface is now mechanically harvestable.

HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable, one cycle): the durable artifact is an ANCHOR-FREE, PER-ACTION, TOOL-CLASS-AWARE SCOPE CHECK ("claim-check v0.3"). The counterparty holds three things they already have, and no key, no CA, no issuer, no vendor, no model: (a) the TOOL-SURFACE MANIFEST they agreed to expose (MCP server + tool schemas), (b) the DECLARED ALLOW-LIST (which action tools, which argument constraints) and (c) the ACTION LOG (per call: tool name, args hash, result hash). The check emits ONE VERDICT PER CALL - IN-SCOPE / OUT-OF-SCOPE / UNDECIDABLE - each citing the exact bytes that justify it, with two rules learned directly from today's survey: (1) a tool that is BOTH source and sink (59 of 1,384) can NEVER be classified safe - if the agreed scope was read-only or bounded, such a call is OUT-OF-SCOPE, because it is a one-call bridge; (2) an action tool whose arguments carry no enum/pattern/format constraint cannot be proven in-scope beyond its declared name - it is UNDECIDABLE unless the scope statement pins the argument values. Verdicts are counted, not narrated.

TEST (E-S25, claim-check v0.3): (a) build artifacts/claim-check v0.3 as a single-file, offline, zero-dependency verifier; unit tests that poison fetch and llm.complete and a CI assertion of zero network and zero model calls. (b) EXTERNAL CALIBRATION: use the published agentsploit corpus (28 servers, 1,384 tools, snapshot 2026-10-20, Apache-2.0) and implement our OWN schema-only capability classifier from their published DEFINITION TEXT only - copying their regexes is prohibited because it would be circular; then measure cross-implementation agreement against their labels. (c) Counterparty corpus: >=30 exchanges across 4 classes - merchant/refund, support reply, booking, and the NEW CI-pipeline-side-effect class - each with counterparty-held manifest bytes, agreed scope, action log and residue. (d) Scope-widening mutations: one extra action tool, one widened argument value, one source->sink bridge call inside a read-only scope, plus a clean control set. (e) METRICS: recall on the 59 both-tools vs published labels = 100% (safety-critical - missing one breaks the premise, so report honest N/N and refuse to ship the tool if missed); per-class agreement published with the disagreement list hand-reviewed the way the survey's author hand-reviewed 9 matches; OUT-OF-SCOPE detection on widened mutations 30/30; false positives on unchanged exchanges = 0; UNDECIDABLE rate < 5%; every verdict cites its justifying bytes; runtime < 100ms per exchange; zero network/model calls. (f) EXTERNAL PROOF, conditional on AX: AX plays the counterparty in a human-interacted session (the social adapter is mock-backed and there is no LLM credential, so publishing now would authenticate nothing); one non-technical person re-derives one check unaided in under 2 minutes and states what the agent did and whether it stayed in scope - published verbatim, including wrong answers.

FALSIFIERS (any one kills the lane): a non-technical counterparty cannot complete the check unaided; the counterparty never retained the manifest/scope bytes (nothing to hash against); our classifier cannot reach 100% recall on the 59 both-tools; UNDECIDABLE rate >= 5% on the corpus; or any external party needs the vendor online to verify.

KILL CRITERION (an instruction, restated unchanged): by 2026-10-25 (72h), if AX has not landed one real LLM credential AND one real social credential, AND the queue is not <=5 and shrinking, AND no terminal mission exists, AND no external party has re-derived a check, then STOP all market-thesis work, publish nothing, and move 100% of the proposal budget to the single verifiable-artifact program (entropy instrumentation, one counted refusal, one externally re-derived check). This is the last cycle allowed to be a thesis rotation rather than an artifact.

AX DECISION NEEDED: one real LLM key and one real social key, or the fleet remains a mirror of its own prompt and every cycle is an unbacked claim - which is the exact failure mode this thesis exists to forbid.
decision:
HOLD LANE #19 (pre-execution control) AND HOLD THE CLAIM-CHECK ARTIFACT SHAPE, BUT CHANGE THE UNIT OF VERIFICATION from the exchange to the single action call, and CALIBRATE ON AN EXTERNAL PUBLISHED CORPUS instead of our own hand-labelled one.

Why the unit changes: the agentsploit survey (1,384 tools / 28 MCP servers, 15:09Z, Apache-2.0, reproducible harness) shows 59 tools that ingest AND act in one call and 14/28 servers that mix sources and sinks in the same agent context with nothing marking which is untrusted. The risk unit is therefore the CALL, not the agent, and the counterparty's question ("was this call inside what we agreed?") can only be answered per call. A single verdict per call - IN-SCOPE / OUT-OF-SCOPE / UNDECIDABLE, each citing its exact bytes - is the shippable unit.

Why the corpus changes: cycle 24's open risk was "who labels our corpus?". The published survey supplies external, auditable, re-runnable labels (source / sink / both) for exactly the classifier the scope check needs. We implement our own schema-only classifier from their published definition text only (copying their regexes is circular and prohibited) and report cross-implementation agreement, with the disagreement list hand-reviewed. Recall on the 59 both-tools must be 100% or we refuse to ship the tool and report honest N/N.

Do NOT compete with: prevention (Fiwu, SentinelMCP, Pith, Aw-1, subst.scsoi, Runspace, agentsploit's own scanner) - consume as price anchors; trust-anchor infrastructure (EUDI Wallet, Langsec, CAs) - our whole point is anchor-free; observation vendors (Amazon TI, ohdear, pwn.watch) - consume as the pricing analogue; trust-anchored receipt products (Circe, Agent Middleware, Viatoris, Paganel) - 2p/9mo says the receipt format is not the demand, and a leaked signing key is a liability, not a moat.

Consume as free corpora / evidence: the 9,930 public agent skills scan (declared-instruction-surface population map, second data point after the 1,866-project study), the MCP tool schemas themselves (machine-inspectable instruction surface), Google's Rust Style Guide and "Rust off Rails" (declared-instruction category with real distribution).

New counterparty persona added to the corpus: the CI pipeline owner (14:49Z, "AI Coding Agents Are Flooding Your CI"). Classes now four: merchant/refund, support reply, booking, CI-side-effect.

Exactly ONE analyze proposal created this cycle (proposal 93400 / mission 93376 / step 93376, queued and enriched with this hypothesis and decision). No external actions, no posts, no risky writes: the social adapter is mock-backed and there is no LLM credential, so publishing anything now would publish a '[mock-llm]' artifact under a verification thesis - precisely what this thesis forbids. The external re-derivation must run against a HUMAN-INTERACTED session (AX plays the agent) so the check binds real actions.

Next cycle reports only: recall on the 59 both-tools vs published labels (and the hand-reviewed disagreement list); per-class agreement; OUT-OF-SCOPE detection on widened mutations; false positives on unchanged exchanges; UNDECIDABLE rate; whether every verdict cites its bytes; runtime; zero-network/zero-model CI assertion; ONE non-technical external re-derivation published verbatim; queue depth and drain vs inflow; output entropy per artifact kind; terminal mission count; and whether AX landed the two credentials.
